reason: This passage from Exodus (the plagues narrative) describes Pharaoh's refusal to release the Israelites despite increasingly devastating plagues sent by God. Pharaoh's governance is explicitly presented as dysfunctional and harmful to his own people—Egypt suffers catastrophic afflictions (frogs, flies, boils, hail, locusts, and darkness) as a direct consequence of his refusal to obey God's command. The text depicts his hardened heart and stubborn resistance to just demands, resulting in widespread suffering among the Egyptian population. Rather than exemplifying 'good leadership to the benefit of the people,' the passage illustrates the opposite: a ruler whose intransigence brings calamity upon his nation. The text is not prescriptive about leadership models but rather narrative of divine judgment and the consequences of unjust governance.
